1. Scope and governing rules
This policy applies to individual transient reservations made through an AuroraStay website, call center, property,
authorized travel advisor, or approved online travel agency. The reservation confirmation controls when it contains a rate
rule that is more specific than this baseline. Group, negotiated corporate, government, wholesale, crew, and extended-stay
agreements may have separate written terms.
The reservation record must show the property, arrival and departure dates, room type, number of guests, rate plan,
payment method, cancellation deadline, taxes and disclosed fees. Staff must read the exact rate plan before promising a
cancellation, change, refund, upgrade, or fee waiver.
Guest-facing summary
Flexible rates can normally be canceled by 6:00 PM local property time one day before arrival without a room
charge. Advance Purchase rates are generally non-refundable and cannot be changed. The confirmation controls if
it states a different rule.

3. Changes, no-shows, and special circumstances
A guest may request a date, room type, occupancy, or property change. Staff must price the modified reservation using the
current available rate and verify whether the original rate plan permits the change. A modification is not complete until the
new confirmation is issued.
If a guest does not arrive by the property cutoff, the reservation is treated as a no-show unless the guest has arranged a
late arrival. The baseline charge is one night plus applicable tax for flexible rates. A multi-night reservation may be released
after the first night unless the property has received payment or written notice for the rest of the stay.
If a property cannot honor a confirmed reservation because of an overbooking or an operational closure, the manager on
duty must arrange a comparable room when feasible, cover approved reasonable relocation costs, and document the

If a property cannot honor a confirmed reservation because of an overbooking or an operational closure, the manager on
duty must arrange a comparable room when feasible, cover approved reasonable relocation costs, and document the
resolution. The manager must not describe a relocation as a guest cancellation.
A manager may approve a one-time exception for a documented service failure, duplicate booking, verified system error, or
other approved service recovery. The reason, approver, amount, and guest communication must be recorded in the
reservation record.

1. Purpose and guest standard
AuroraStay wants a safe, clean, and welcoming stay for guests, visitors, and staff. These guidelines apply in guest rooms,
public areas, parking areas, meeting spaces, and property-operated transportation. They supplement the reservation
terms, posted notices, emergency instructions, and applicable law.
Staff should address conduct concerns early, use neutral language, and apply rules consistently. A staff member should
not confront a guest alone when there is a safety risk. Contact the manager on duty or emergency services according to
the severity of the situation.
Immediate safety rule
Call 911 for an immediate threat to life, serious injury, fire, active violence, or suspected crime in progress. Notify the
manager on duty when safe. Do not delay emergency care to complete a complaint record.

3. Accessibility and service animals
AuroraStay follows the Americans with Disabilities Act Title III requirements for places of lodging and provides reasonable
modifications and accessible features as required by applicable law. Staff should focus on the requested feature or task,
not on the guest's diagnosis or private medical information.

A guest reports discrimination

channel. Escalate urgent safety or access concerns immediately.
Staff must not demand a service animal certificate, vest, or medical record as a condition of entry. Service animals are not
subject to a pet fee. A direct threat assessment must be based on objective evidence and an individualized assessment,
not on stereotypes.

4. Safety, privacy, and lost property
Guests should use the room safe when available and keep keys, mobile credentials, and personal information secure. Staff
verify identity before issuing a replacement key, providing room information, or releasing stored luggage. Staff must not
announce a guest's room number aloud in public.
Lost property is logged, secured, and returned through the approved process. Staff should not open, browse, or share
personal content from a found device except as needed to identify the owner through an approved procedure. Suspected
weapons, drugs, exploitation, or immediate danger are handled through safety escalation, not informal investigation.

1. Purpose and refund principles
This guide helps guest service staff explain refunds, releases, credits, and additional charges. The reservation rate terms
control eligibility. The payment method and booking channel control how the money moves. Staff must not promise a
refund before checking both.
Refunds generally return to the original payment method. A different method may be used only when Finance or a
manager approves it and the transaction can be documented. Cash refunds are not the default for card or agency
payments.
Three questions before quoting a refund
What was charged? What rule makes it refundable or non-refundable? Who can release or approve the funds? If
any answer is unclear, say that the request is under review and give the guest a follow-up channel.

4. Incidentals authorization and release
At arrival, the property may authorize an amount for anticipated incidentals. The authorization can reduce available credit
without being a posted charge. When the folio is settled, the property sends a release for the unused amount. The card
issuer controls how quickly the pending hold disappears; AuroraStay cannot guarantee a same-day release.
If a guest sees a pending hold after checkout, staff should confirm the final folio, explain that the unused portion was

If a guest sees a pending hold after checkout, staff should confirm the final folio, explain that the unused portion was
released or is scheduled for release, and advise the guest to contact the card issuer if the pending status persists beyond
the issuer's normal timeframe. A pending authorization is not evidence of a second final charge.

4. Parking, pets, and service animals
Parking is not guaranteed unless the reservation or property profile says it is reserved. Staff must quote the current parking
type and charge, explain whether in-and-out access is allowed, and tell the guest how to validate or pay. Parking charges
are separate from the room rate unless the confirmation says they are included.
Pet rules are property-specific. A pet fee, weight limit, number limit, room restriction, and vaccination or control requirement

Pet rules are property-specific. A pet fee, weight limit, number limit, room restriction, and vaccination or control requirement
may apply. Service animals are not pets under the ADA and are not subject to a pet fee. Staff may ask only the two
ADA-permitted questions when the disability-related need is not obvious: whether the animal is required because of a
disability and what work or task it has been trained to perform.
An emotional support, comfort, or therapy animal that does not meet the ADA service animal definition is handled under the
property's pet rule unless another law or approved accommodation applies. Do not request a certificate, vest, or medical
record as a condition of recognizing a service animal.

6. Accessibility and guest requests
AuroraStay provides reasonable modifications and accessible features as required by applicable law. A guest may request
an accessible route, mobility feature, visual or audible alert, communication support, or another accommodation. Staff
should ask what feature is needed, record the request in the approved system, and confirm what the property can provide.
Do not treat a request for an accessible room as an optional preference when the guest is asking for an accessibility
feature. Do not disclose the guest's disability details to staff who do not need them. If the request cannot be met as stated,
involve the manager on duty and offer a specific alternative without making a promise the property cannot deliver.
Service animals may accompany a guest in areas open to guests, subject to the ADA rules for control, housebreaking, and
direct threat. A property may remove an animal that is out of control or not housebroken when the issue is not corrected,

Escalate immediately
Escalate a request when a guest reports a blocked accessible route, an inaccessible room feature, a service animal
dispute, a safety risk, or a potential discrimination complaint. Record the request and the response in neutral factual
language.
